Good King accepted the Fairy's promise, and she understood his wishes.
Each assured the other that they would keep their promises: one for kindness
toward all, and one for friendship toward the prince.
Chapter 2 Prince Darling's Ring
Good King was confident of the Fairy's promise, but very soon after their
conversation, he died. His son, Prince Darling, was very sad, for he loved
his father deeply, and would willingly have given all his kingdoms and all his
treasures of gold and silver to keep Good King with him.
Two days after his father's death, the Fairy appeared to Prince Darling as he
got ready for bed. "I promised your father that I would be your friend. To keep
my word, I have come to bring you a present." As she spoke, she put a little
gold ring upon his royal finger.
"Take great care of this ring," she said. "It is more precious than diamonds.
Every time you do a bad deed, it will prick your finger. If, in spite of its
pricking, you continue in your own evil ways, you will lose my friendship, and
I will become your enemy." After these words, the Fairy disappeared, leaving
Prince Darling in shock.
For some time, Prince Darling behaved so well that the ring never pricked
him, and that made him very satisfied with himself. His people loved him too.
They called him "Prince Darling the Happy".
One day, however, Prince Darling the Happy went out hunting. He had
gone back to the hunting ground many times but dich tund any animals. This
made him very upset.
